title: policy multiplexer, audit-proofing, and KMS tag gating for jurisdictional residency
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add Policy Multiplexer service for unified RBAC v2 decisioning and KMS tag gating. Rollout behind feature flag 'policy_mux_enabled' with staged canary. No breaking API changes.
body: Summary: This PR introduces the Policy Multiplexer (policy-mux) - a lightweight decisioning and enforcement facade that consolidates RBAC v2 attributes, per-request residency assertions, and KMS tag gating into a single enforcement path. The mux produces a compact audit envelope attached to requests and emits structured telemetry for residency mismatches and gating events. Motivation: We continue to see combinatorial complexity across operator-scoped roles, tenant attributes, and per-request region pins. Enforcement logic is duplicated across codepaths (serving runtime, private installer, and admin APIs). The policy-mux centralizes three concerns: 1) attribute combination (operator, service, tenant, request claims) for RBAC v2 decisions; 2) KMS tag gating to prevent key usage when residency tags don't match policy; 3) production-friendly audit-proofing where an audit envelope is appended and signed for downstream storage. Design highlights: - New service 'policy-mux' (go) that exposes a gRPC endpoint (PolicyDecision/Enforce) and an HTTP sidecar-compatible adapter for the gateway. - Decision flow: collect attributes -> canonicalize residency headers (X-Redwood-Residency, X-Redwood-Residency-V2) -> consult fast decision cache -> if cached miss, call Policy Engine (PD-API) and merge results. - KMS tag gating: a pluggable gate that checks request.metadata.kms_tags against the allowed tag set derived from policy and tenant config; failing gating will produce an enforce DENY with a structured audit entry. - Audit-proofing: create an immutable audit envelope (base64 JSON) containing decision_id, effective_attributes, kms_gating_result, and a signer reference (service key id). Envelopes are appended as X-Redwood-Audit-Envelope header for synchronous flows and forwarded to audit-writer for async persistence. - Fallback: when policy-mux is unhealthy, requests are routed to legacy/rbacv2-legacy service under a circuit-breaker. This preserves availability while we finish rollout. - Feature flag: 'policy_mux_enabled' (pkg/config/feature_flags.go) defaults to false. Migration and rollout: - Phase 1 (canary): enable policy_mux_enabled in us-west1 for 5% traffic and collect gating metrics. - Phase 2 (expand): enable for all internal dev clusters, monitor error rates and audit envelope rejections. - Phase 3: global gradual enable, switch default gateway route to policy-mux with fallback disabled once metrics are stable. Backwards compatibility: - No surface API changes. Audit envelope header is additive. KMS gating denies are explicit and return 403 with an audit envelope explaining decision. Testing: - Unit tests cover attribute merge logic, residency reconciliation, and KMS gating edge cases. - Integration: smoke tests in e2e/policy_mux_smoke.yml exercise gateway + kms-proxy interactions. - Chaos: simulated policy engine latency and audit-writer outages to validate circuit-breaker and fallback. Observability and alerts: - New metrics: policy_mux.requests_total, policy_mux.denied_kms_tag_mismatch_total, policy_mux.audit_envelope_failures_total, policy_mux.cache_hit_ratio. - Dashboards: observability/dashboards/policy_mux.json added. - SLOs: maintain p95 decision latency <12ms on canary hardware; alert if p95 > 50ms or error rate > 0.5%. Security review: - KMS gating uses tenant-scoped tag allowlist derived from tenant metadata and CMK origin context. - Audit envelope signer uses ephemeral service key rotated by the operator key manager. - Threat model doc appended to docs/rbacv2/policy-mux.md. Checklist: - [x] Feature flag gating implemented - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] E2E smoke - [x] Observability metrics and dashboard - [x] Security review sign-off (SEC-511) - [x] Canary rollout plan - [x] Documentation updated (docs/rbacv2/policy-mux.md) Migration script: included scripts/migrate/rbac-mapping-fallbacks.sql to add light-weight fallbacks mapping for legacy role aliases. Rollback plan: flip feature flag policy_mux_enabled=false; gateway routes automatically revert to rbacv2-legacy; run cleanup task to drop ephemeral audit envelopes if necessary. Operational notes: - On gating DENYs, ops will see structured audit reason 'kms_tag_mismatch' with an offending tag list. - We intentionally do not auto-escalate to operators; DENYs require tenant/ops review to update tag allowlist. Related work: ENG-2403 (policy consolidation), SEC-511 (audit-proofing spec), OPS-92 (canary plan).

review_comments: Ethan Ross: Can we add unit coverage for the 'mixed-residency' header case where both X-Redwood-Residency and X-Redwood-Residency-V2 are present? I'd prefer deterministic precedence in tests.
Maya Chen (author): Added unit tests and a comment in attribute_merger.go explaining precedence: V2 wins over legacy header. See internal/rbac/v2/attribute_merger.go:45-62.
Priya Patel: KMS gating looks good. Two asks: (1) show expected error payload shape for 403 responses, (2) ensure signer key id is not emitted in plain text to logs.

Maya Chen (author): Addressed both. Error payload shape included in docs/rbacv2/policy-mux.md and signer key id is redacted in logs; audit envelope contains signer reference id only, not raw key material.
Liam O'Connor: Observability: please add cache hit ratio metric and an alert for cache degradation. Also verify HPA settings for policy-mux pod CPU burn.
Maya Chen (author): Added policy_mux.cache_hit_ratio and alert rule; set HPA target to 60% CPU with conservative min=2/max=12 for canary stage.
